descriptionAdvanced.en: Tambo Quemado is the busiest and most strategic international border post in Bolivia, situated at a high altitude of over 4,600 meters in the Oruro Department. It serves as the primary gateway for the country's international trade, handling thousands of trucks daily that carry minerals and agricultural products to the Chilean port of Arica and bring back manufactured goods and fuel. The crossing is located in a starkly beautiful volcanic landscape at the foot of the massive Sajama volcano. Due to its vital role, the facility is equipped with specialized customs and immigration services that operate under extreme weather conditions, including intense cold and wind. Historically, this route has been the preferred path for Bolivian trade since colonial times, and today it is the essential artery connecting the heart of the Andes with the global market.

en: Tambo Quemado handles more than 60% of Bolivia's international land-based cargo traffic.
The crossing is part of the important international highway that connects La Paz with the Pacific coast.
The thin air and freezing temperatures make it one of the most challenging working environments for customs officers in the world.
It is located within the buffer zone of the Sajama National Park.
